newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem warns of lower 1997 profits.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem warns of lower 1997 profits.

text.p: South African chemical company Sentrachem Ltd on Thursday said losses in its Sanachem subsidiary would impact substantially on group profitability in the 1997 financial year.

Sentrachem said in a published announcement it had become clear that the profitability of Sanachem, which accounted for 10 percent of the group's operating profit last year, had been severely compromised.
The unrealised loss, which was non-recurring, would now be brought to account, it said.

Sanachem's operating performance was expected to be well below that of last year mainly due to the company being burdened by forward exchange contracts representing 18 months of export trade. A profit forecast was being reviewed but no finality had yet been reached, the announcement said.
"The Sentrachem group, therefore, has decided to announce that the impact of these issues on the group profitability in the 1997 financial year will be substantial," it said.
It said the impact of the forward contracts would be 60 cents a share.
Once greater certainty had been reached, the anticipated impact of Sanachem's perfomance on group earnings would be made known, Sentrachem said.
The other four group companies, U.S.-based Hampshire Chemical Corp, Karbochem, NCP and Safripol, were continuing to show improved operating performances compared with last year.
Shareholders were advised to exercise caution in their sharedealings.
